Make tests/test_member_friction.py::test_unnamed_dispatch_is_admitted_while_a_review_worker_is_alive assert only what it can cause. Its fixture teardown currently asserts _real_stores() == before. That compares the whole real crew store, including live run pointers and records, before and after the test. On a shared host, peer sessions dispatch during any suite run, so it errors in both arms of a merge check. It did so in the 2026-10-07 subscription-lanes merge check (~/.cache/reckon-suite-logs/merge-subscription-lanes-base.log and -head.log), and passed alone in a quiet window.

1. Keep the guard's purpose: the test must not write into the real crew home. Check that by what the test itself could write, not by the whole store standing still. For example, assert that no entry under the real store names the fixture's project, member or run ids, or snapshot the real store and allow only entries that do not belong to this test.
2. Prove the guard still catches a real leak. A variant of the test that deliberately writes one fixture-named entry into the real store must fail the guard. Clean that entry up in the variant itself.
3. Prove it tolerates peers. A test that writes an unrelated entry into the real store's view during the fixture, standing in for a peer dispatch, must pass, and clean up after itself. Run all of this under a temporary RECKON_HOME that stands in for the real store, so the suite never writes the real home.
4. Negative control: restoring the whole-store equality makes the peer-tolerance test fail.

Write only tests/test_member_friction.py and the evidence fragment. Gate: tests/test_member_friction.py and tests/test_dispatch*.py. Run with the main checkout's .venv/bin/python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -n 6 in the FOREGROUND, with one log each for base and head under the run directory, each ending in an EXIT line, judged by delta. Write the evidence fragment docs/evidence/fragments/one-typesafe-model-picker/member-friction-asserts-its-own-writes.html.
